en: Jātaka:
The Eighth Chapter, the Section on Kaccāyana (Aṭṭhakanipāta Kaccānivagga)
2. The Aṭṭhasadda Jātaka “This place was formerly called ‘Sloping Down,’ with its abundant fish and great waters;”
This is the dwelling of the king of frogs, my ancestral abode;
let us subsist here on frogs.
"We do not abandon our home.
"Who will be able to break the bond of one who is unvirtuous and lacks strength?"
“Who will protect my children in their nest, and ensure my own safety? “All the heartwood has been consumed;
there is only sapwood remaining.”
Such was her fate,
O Great King: when its food is exhausted,
a wood-boring beetle finds no delight in the heartwood.
“Surely, having gone from here,
released from the king’s residence,
I shall delight myself.”
“Dumasākhaniketinī. “Surely, having gone from here,
I shall be released from the king’s residence;”
“I shall drink the first water;
I shall lead the herd at the front.
“Thus, you have become perfectly intoxicated with sensual pleasures.”
Red with passion, infatuated with sensual desires—
the fierce Bhaddiya the Bāhika has brought you here.
May it be well with you!
“In this thick darkness on the high upper mountain,
she [comforted] me with her gentle and soft [words].”
"Do not let your foot slip on the gravel.
"Without doubt, having seen the destruction of birth,
I shall not enter a womb again."
“This is my final, last bed in a womb;
my cycle of existence for further becoming is exhausted.
The Second Jātaka of the Eight Sounds.
